title: Govinda Warns of Rs 100 Crore Legal Action Over False Marriage and Divorce Claims
excerpt: The veteran Bollywood actor issues a public notice targeting media outlets and content creators days after wife Sunita Ahuja withdrew her divorce petition.
body:
• Bollywood actor Govinda has issued a public notice threatening Rs 100 crore in damages against anyone spreading false claims about a court marriage and divorce with wife Sunita Ahuja.
  • The notice comes days after Sunita withdrew the divorce case she had filed against the actor at Bandra Family Court in December 2024.
  • Govinda's legal team has warned of civil and criminal proceedings under defamation and IT laws against content creators and media outlets propagating fabricated reports.
  • The couple, married since 1987, has weathered months of public speculation fueled by reality TV appearances, social media posts, and unverified court document leaks.

Govinda Issues Formal Legal Warning

https://youtube.com/watch?v=_83yKVzVRCE

Bollywood actor Govinda has issued a public notice warning of Rs 100 crore in damages against individuals and media outlets spreading what he calls fabricated reports about his personal life, according to reports in The Economic Times, Hindustan Times, and Telegraph India.

The notice specifically targets claims about an alleged court marriage and divorce proceedings with his wife of nearly four decades, Sunita Ahuja. Govinda's legal team has stated that civil and criminal proceedings will be initiated under relevant defamation and information technology laws against anyone creating or disseminating such content.

"His team will pursue civil and criminal actions against offenders under relevant laws."

— Govinda's legal team, via public notice

Divorce Case Withdrawn Days Earlier

The public notice follows a significant development on August 19, when Sunita Ahuja reportedly withdrew the divorce case she had filed against Govinda. The withdrawal was confirmed by the actor's manager, Shashi Sinha, in a statement to NDTV.

https://x.com/ZoomTV/status/2091417955318001975

Sunita had filed the divorce petition at Mumbai's Bandra Family Court on December 5, 2024, under Sections 13(1)(i), (ia), and (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — legal provisions that correspond to allegations of adultery, cruelty, and desertion.

The court summoned Govinda, but he did not appear in person until a formal notice to show cause was issued in May 2025. Court-mandated counseling sessions began in June 2025, with Sunita attending hearings in person. It remained unclear whether Govinda participated in the sessions virtually or in person.

A Timeline of Public Speculation

The couple's marital troubles became tabloid fodder starting in late 2024. Social media posts, emotional YouTube vlogs by Sunita, and Reddit threads fueled a cycle of speculation that persisted for over a year.

In February 2025, Govinda's manager Shashi Sinha dismissed the divorce reports as a "publicity stunt," telling IANS that while a legal notice had been filed, there was "no concrete matter" behind it. The family reunited publicly during Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations in August 2025, with Sunita telling media, "No one can separate us, not even if God or a devil comes down."

But the issue resurfaced. In March 2026, Govinda responded to Sunita's allegations of infidelity, saying he did not want to "publicly embarrass anyone" and chose to keep his side private. The situation escalated further when Sunita spoke about alleged infidelity during her appearance on the reality show Lock Upp: Sach Ya Sazaa, saying she had been hurt but that her children remained her priority.

Govinda himself addressed the situation in an earlier ANI interview, describing what he called a "big conspiracy" in which family members were being "used" without their knowledge.

"Sometimes when we don't speak, we either appear weak or it seems like we are simply the problem. So, today, I'm responding."

— Govinda, in an interview with ANI

Son's Bollywood Debut Adds Family Context

The legal warning arrives at a busy moment for the Ahuja family. Govinda's son Yashvardhan Ahuja has recently locked his Bollywood debut, with reports indicating the entire family is on board for the project. The timing of the public notice suggests Govinda is looking to draw a line under the personal controversies before the family enters a new phase of public visibility.

Shashi Sinha, speaking about the divorce withdrawal, said he felt the matter "did not need to reach the courts or become a public spectacle," adding that disagreements happen in families and many issues can be resolved through conversation.

What the Legal Notice Means

The Rs 100 crore damages figure, while large, is not uncommon in Indian celebrity defamation cases — it signals intent more than a specific monetary claim. What makes Govinda's notice notable is its explicit targeting of content creators and social media accounts, reflecting how speculation about celebrity personal lives has increasingly migrated from tabloid pages to Instagram reels, YouTube vlogs, and anonymous Reddit threads.

Govinda and Sunita married on March 11, 1987. They have two children — daughter Tina Ahuja, who has appeared in Bollywood, and son Yashvardhan. The actor, known for his iconic comedy roles in films like Haseena Maan Jaayegi and Partner, has faced a series of personal and professional challenges in recent years, including an accidental self-inflicted gunshot wound in October 2024 and involvement as a witness in a Ponzi scheme investigation.

Whether the public notice leads to actual legal proceedings remains to be seen. But the message from Govinda's camp is clear: the actor considers the chapter closed and is prepared to use the courts against anyone who disagrees.
